paper.title_en: Elastic scattering, inelastic excitations and one-neutron stripping transfer reaction of the $^{13}$C+$^{64}$Zn system at energies around the Coulomb barrier
paper.abstract_en: This work presents new experimental data for the elastic scattering, the inelastic excitations and one-neutron (1n) transfer angular distributions of $^{13}$C on $^{64}$Zn, at energies around the Coulomb barrier ($V_{B}\approx $ 30 MeV). Data were obtained at four bombarding energies: $E_\text {lab}$ = 28, 30, 33 and 36 MeV. The corresponding optical model (OM) analysis, based on the São Paulo Optical Model Protocol (SP-OMP), and the microscopic coupled-channels calculations are also presented. We determine the best-fit ($\chi _\text {red}^2$) optical potentials (OPs), which are then applied to the CC/CRC calculations. The OM and CC/CRC calculations are compared to the experimental elastic and non-elastic angular distributions obtained for the $^{13}$C+$^{64}$Zn system. The SP-OMP effectively describes the elastic scattering cross sections of $^{13}$C+$^{64}$Zn. The CC/CRC calculations corroborate the OM analysis, reproducing non-elastic nuclear reaction data. These calculations highlight the main importance of taking into account the excited states of the $^{64}$Zn target along the energy range, in addition to coupling the excited states and the one neutron stripping of the $^{13}$C projectile, as the bombarding energy increases. Comparisons between $^{12,13}$C+$^{64}$Zn are also proposed. Differences due to the $^{13}$C extra neutron could be inferred.
